MEMO
To: All staff, Harrowgate Tile Company
From: Delphine Arkwright, Operations Director
Date: 3 February
Subject: Warehouse move to Pellam Road

As many of you have heard, our lease on the Quarry Lane warehouse ends this spring, and the board has approved a move to a larger unit at 14 Pellam Road. This memo sets out the schedule, what each team needs to do, and how the move affects deliveries.

Why we are moving. The Quarry Lane building has 2,400 square metres of floor space, and for most of last year we have also been renting overflow storage from a neighbouring business. The Pellam Road unit has 3,900 square metres, a covered loading bay with four dock doors instead of two, and is 6 kilometres closer to the motorway junction. The monthly rent at Pellam Road is higher, at 18,200 pounds compared with 12,750 pounds at Quarry Lane today, but once we move we will stop paying the 3,100 pounds a month for the overflow storage.

Schedule. Packing of slow-moving stock (anything not ordered in the last 90 days) begins on Monday 3 March. The main move will take place over the weekend of 15 and 16 March. Quarry Lane will close for customer collections on Friday 14 March at noon, and Pellam Road will open for collections on Tuesday 18 March at 8 a.m. There will be no collections on Monday 17 March while the new racking is inspected.

Teams. The dispatch team, led by Owen Castellan, is responsible for labelling every pallet with its new aisle and bay code. The sales team, led by Priya Venn, will contact every trade customer with an open order before 7 March. The finance team, led by Marcus Hale, will handle the transfer of electricity, water and phone accounts. Anyone who uses a personal locker at Quarry Lane must empty it by 12 March; lockers at the new site will be assigned by the dispatch team.

Deliveries. Outbound deliveries will pause from 13 March to 17 March inclusive. Orders placed during that window will be shipped in the order they were received, starting 18 March.

Budget. The board approved a moving budget of 46,000 pounds, which covers the removal firm, new racking, and signage. We have set aside 5,000 pounds of that for unexpected costs.

Parking. Pellam Road has 38 staff parking spaces. Because we have 52 staff, a parking rota will be published by the end of February.

Update, 10 February: Following the racking survey, the removal firm has revised its quote, and the board has raised the moving budget to 51,500 pounds. The 5,000 pounds set aside for unexpected costs is unchanged. In addition, the landlord at Pellam Road has agreed to a three-month rent-free period, so the first rent payment will be due in June rather than March.

Update, 24 February: The racking inspection has been moved forward, so Pellam Road will now open for customer collections on Monday 17 March at 8 a.m. The delivery pause is unchanged. The parking rota has been published on the staff noticeboard.

Please direct any questions to Delphine or to your team lead.
passages.p02:
RESIDENTIAL TENANCY AGREEMENT - KEY TERMS SUMMARY
Property: Flat 7B, Linnet House, 22 Carrow Street, Mossbridge
Landlord: Fenwick Holdings Ltd, represented by managing agent Tamsin Oduya
Tenants: Rafael Quint and Ingrid Salo
All amounts are in pounds.

1. Term. The tenancy begins on 1 September 2025 and runs for a fixed term of 18 months. After the fixed term, it continues from month to month until either party gives notice.

2. Rent. Rent is 1,340 per month, payable in advance on the 1st of each month by bank transfer. The first month's rent is due on signing. Rent will not be increased during the fixed term. After the fixed term, the landlord may increase the rent no more than once in any 12-month period, with at least 60 days' written notice.

3. Late payment. If rent has not been received by the end of the 5th day of the month, a late fee of 45 is charged. A further 5 is added for each additional day the rent remains unpaid after that, up to a maximum total late fee of 120 for any one month.

4. Deposit. The tenants will pay a security deposit of 1,850, which will be held in a government-approved deposit scheme. The deposit will be returned within 21 days of the end of the tenancy, less any agreed deductions.

5. Pets. No pets are permitted without the landlord's written consent, with the following exceptions: assistance dogs, fish kept in a tank of up to 60 litres, and one caged bird. Any other animal, including cats, rabbits and dogs other than assistance dogs, requires written consent and an additional pet deposit of 300.

6. Utilities. The tenants are responsible for electricity, gas, broadband and council tax. Water and building insurance are included in the rent. Lighting in the communal hallway is paid for by the landlord.

7. Repairs. The tenants must report any repair need within 7 days of noticing it. Urgent repairs (no heating or hot water between October and April, a leak through a ceiling, or a front door that will not lock) will be attended to within 24 hours. Non-urgent repairs will be attended to within 14 days.

8. Ending the tenancy. During the fixed term, the tenants may end the tenancy early only by finding a replacement tenant approved by the landlord, and must pay a re-letting fee of 250. After the fixed term, the tenants must give one month's notice and the landlord must give two months' notice.

9. Parking. One allocated parking space (space number 31) is included in the rent. A second space may be rented for 40 per month, subject to availability.

10. Decoration. Tenants may hang pictures using small nails or adhesive hooks. Painting walls requires written consent. Any walls that are painted must be returned to the original colour, Linen White, at the end of the tenancy unless the landlord agrees otherwise.

11. Smoking. Smoking and vaping are not permitted anywhere inside the flat or in the communal areas. Smoking is allowed on the flat's balcony only if the balcony door is kept closed.

Signed on 18 August 2025 by both tenants and by Tamsin Oduya on behalf of the landlord.
passages.p03:
ITINERARY - NORTHERN COAST PHOTOGRAPHY TOUR
Travellers: 12 members of the Brisk Lane Photography Club
Tour leader: Joaquim Ferris (mobile 0770 214 889)
Prepared by: Saltmarsh Travel, booking reference ST-4471

Overview. The tour runs for seven days, from Saturday 9 May to Friday 15 May, and visits three towns on the northern coast: Port Allard, Veyra, and Callowmere. All travel between towns is by chartered minibus unless stated otherwise. The price per person is 1,180, which includes accommodation in twin rooms, breakfasts, the minibus, the ferry crossings, the lighthouse visit, the long-exposure workshop and the ranger-led walk. Lunches and dinners are not included, except the welcome dinner on Day 1 and the farewell dinner on Day 6.

Day 1 - Saturday 9 May: Arrival in Port Allard. Meet at Holt Street coach station at 07:45 for the 08:15 coach to Port Allard (journey time 3 hours 40 minutes). Check in at the Gull and Anchor Hotel, 3 Wharf Row, from 14:00. At 16:30, Joaquim will lead a short orientation walk along the harbour wall, about 2 km in total. The welcome dinner is at 19:30 in the hotel's Lantern Room.

Day 2 - Sunday 10 May: Port Allard harbour and lighthouse. At 05:40 there is an optional sunrise shoot at the harbour mouth for anyone who wants it; meet in the hotel lobby. Breakfast is served from 07:00. At 10:00, a guided visit to Tarrant Point Lighthouse, climbing 164 steps to the lamp gallery. Tripods are not allowed inside the lighthouse, but may be used on the outside platform. The afternoon is free. We recommend the fish market on the north quay, which closes at 13:00 on Sundays.

Day 3 - Monday 11 May: Transfer to Veyra. Check out of the Gull and Anchor by 09:30. The minibus leaves at 10:00 for Veyra, a drive of about 95 km with a stop at the Selkie Bay viewpoint. We expect to arrive around 13:00 and check in at the Veyra Mill Guesthouse. At 15:00 there is a workshop on long-exposure technique with local photographer Anneli Brook, held in the guesthouse barn. Each participant should bring a neutral density filter if they have one; the club has four spare filters to lend.

Day 4 - Tuesday 12 May: Veyra salt flats. The minibus leaves at 06:15 for the salt flats, a drive of 35 minutes each way. We return for a late breakfast at 09:30. At 14:00 there is an optional visit to the Veyra Weaving Museum; entry costs 8 and is not included in the tour price. The evening is free, and the guesthouse can recommend several restaurants within walking distance.

Day 5 - Wednesday 13 May: Ferry to Callowmere. The minibus takes the group to Veyra pier for the 11:20 ferry to Callowmere Island. The crossing takes 1 hour 50 minutes. Luggage stays in the minibus, which travels on the vehicle deck of the same ferry. On arrival, check in at the Callowmere Harbour Inn. In the late afternoon, there is a seabird colony walk with ranger Petra Holm, 4.5 km over rough ground; sturdy boots are required.

Day 6 - Thursday 14 May: Callowmere. The morning is free. At 13:00 there is the portfolio review in the inn's function room, where each member presents five images taken during the tour and Anneli Brook, who is travelling to the island for the day, gives feedback. At 19:00 the farewell dinner is held at the Old Customs House restaurant.

Day 7 - Friday 15 May: Return. The group takes the 08:40 ferry back to Veyra pier, then the minibus to Holt Street coach station, arriving at approximately 16:00.

Rooms. Twin rooms are standard. A single-room supplement of 210 per person applies for the whole tour. The Veyra Mill Guesthouse has only three single rooms, which will be allocated in order of booking; anyone who pays the supplement but cannot be given a single room in Veyra will receive a refund of 60.

Payments. A deposit of 250 per person was due on booking. The balance is due 6 weeks before departure. Cancellations made more than 6 weeks before departure lose the deposit only; cancellations after that point lose 50 percent of the total price; cancellations within 7 days of departure lose the full price. Travel insurance is strongly recommended and is not included.

Change notice, 20 April: The ferry company has revised its timetable. The Day 5 ferry to Callowmere now departs at 12:05 instead of 11:20; the crossing time is unchanged. The Day 7 return ferry now departs at 09:10 instead of 08:40, and the expected arrival at Holt Street coach station is now approximately 16:30.

What to pack. Warm layers, a waterproof jacket, sturdy boots for Day 5, a head torch for the Day 2 sunrise shoot, spare memory cards, and chargers. The Callowmere Harbour Inn has limited power sockets in its rooms, so please bring a small extension lead if you can. Drones may not be flown at the seabird colony or at the lighthouse.

Emergency contacts. In an emergency during the tour, call Joaquim first. If he cannot be reached, call the Saltmarsh Travel 24-hour line on 0161 550 3020 and quote the booking reference ST-4471.
passages.p04:
Laboratory Report LR-2291: Effect of Temperature on the Activity of Corvase-2
Author: Dr Hana Welliver, Brackenfield Institute, Enzymology Group
Assistants: Tomasz Reyl and Ama Dorsey

Aim. To measure how the activity of the enzyme Corvase-2, extracted from cultured Kessel moss, changes with temperature, and to estimate the temperature at which its activity peaks.

Method. Six water baths were set at 20, 30, 37, 45, 55 and 65 degrees Celsius. At each temperature, three test tubes (replicates A, B and C) each received 2.0 mL of substrate solution at 0.5 mol/L and 0.2 mL of enzyme extract. After exactly 10 minutes the reaction was stopped with 1.0 mL of stop reagent, and the amount of product formed was measured in micromoles using a spectrophotometer at 412 nm. Activity is reported as micromoles of product formed per minute, calculated by dividing the product formed by the 10-minute reaction time.

Results. Product formed after 10 minutes, in micromoles:
- 20 °C: A 11.8, B 12.4, C 12.1
- 30 °C: A 20.3, B 19.7, C 20.6
- 37 °C: A 27.5, B 28.1, C 27.8
- 45 °C: A 31.9, B 32.4, C 32.0
- 55 °C: A 18.2, B 17.5, C 18.8
- 65 °C: A 3.1, B 2.8, C 3.4

Note on replicate B at 45 °C: the first attempt was spoiled when the tube cracked in the bath, and replicate B was re-run the same afternoon. The value shown above is from the re-run. The original reading of 40.6 is excluded from all results.

Discussion. Activity rose steadily from 20 °C to 45 °C and fell sharply above 45 °C. The steep fall between 55 °C and 65 °C is consistent with the enzyme being denatured at high temperature. The highest mean product formation was at 45 °C. Tomasz noted that the 55 °C bath drifted up to 56.5 °C for about two minutes during the run, which may have slightly lowered the 55 °C readings. Ama checked the spectrophotometer against a blank before and after the run and found no drift.

Conclusions. Under these conditions, the optimum temperature of Corvase-2 lies between 37 °C and 55 °C, most likely near 45 °C. A follow-up run with baths at 40, 42, 45, 48 and 50 °C is recommended to narrow the estimate.

Storage. The remaining enzyme extract, 14 mL, was stored at 4 °C in fridge 3, shelf B, in a tube labelled CV2-0917. It should be used within 10 days of the run.

Minutes - Kilnworth Community Garden Committee
Date: Wednesday 4 June, 18:30 to 20:15
Location: Kilnworth Library, Room 2
Present: Beatrix Oyelaran (chair), Callum Dray (treasurer), Mei-Lin Pask (secretary), Samir Holloway, Greta Vance, Ivo Brennan
Apologies: Fatima Rudd

1. Minutes of the last meeting. The minutes of the meeting held on 7 May were approved with one correction: the number of people on the plot waiting list was 23, not 32 as written.

2. Treasurer's report. Callum reported a bank balance of 4,860 at 31 May. Income since the last meeting was 1,215, made up of plot fees (960), the spring plant sale (205) and a donation from the Kilnworth Bakery (50). Expenses were 388: a replacement hose reel (74), a compost delivery (290) and postage (24). Callum reminded members that the annual insurance renewal of 610 is due on 1 July. He also noted that four plot holders have not yet paid this year's fees, and he will send them a reminder.

3. Water supply. Greta reported that the main standpipe leaked twice in May and that the south end of the site had no water for three days. The water company has quoted 1,450 to install a new metered supply with two extra taps. Samir suggested collecting rainwater as well: four 1,000-litre tanks, with new guttering on the tool shed and the polytunnel, would cost about 720 in total. After discussion, the committee agreed to do both, but to install the rainwater tanks first and to apply to the council's small grants scheme for the metered supply. The committee voted 5 to 1 in favour. Ivo voted against because he felt the metered supply should come first.

4. Plots. There are 48 plots in total. Of these, 41 are let, 3 are being cleared after their tenants left, and 4 are kept as shared plots for the children's gardening club. Mei-Lin will write to the first three people on the waiting list to offer them the plots being cleared, once the clearing is finished. Plot fees for next year will stay at 40 for a full plot and 25 for a half plot. Concession fees for pensioners and students will be 20 for a full plot, down from 30 this year, and will stay at 15 for a half plot.

5. Open Day. The Open Day will be held on Saturday 19 July from 11:00 to 15:00. Beatrix will contact the local radio station and the parish newsletter. Samir will run the seed swap table. Greta offered to organise a scarecrow competition, with a garden centre voucher worth 30 as the prize. The committee agreed a budget of 300 for the Open Day, to cover posters, refreshments and the voucher. Members agreed that the children's gardening club should have its own stall to sell pressed flowers, with the money going to the club.

6. Tool shed. Ivo reported that the padlock on the tool shed was cut in late May and two strimmers were taken. The theft was reported to the police (crime reference KW-55180). The insurer has said the strimmers are covered, less an excess of 100. The committee agreed to replace the padlock with a combination lock; the new code will be sent by text message to plot holders only and will not be posted on the noticeboard.

7. Composting. Samir said the three compost bays are full and that some plot holders are putting bindweed and diseased potato plants in them. The committee agreed to put up a sign listing what should not go in the bays, and to buy a fourth bay if the budget allows later in the year.

8. Any other business. Greta asked whether small bonfires could be allowed in winter. The committee decided that bonfires remain banned at all times; green waste should go in the compost bays or be taken to the council tip. Beatrix thanked Mei-Lin for redesigning the garden's website, which now lists the plot rules, the compost guidance and a contact form for people who want to join the waiting list. Samir asked that the website also show the dates of the monthly work mornings.

Action items:
- Callum: pay the insurance renewal before 1 July and send fee reminders.
- Samir: get two further quotes for the rainwater tanks by 18 June.
- Mei-Lin: write to the waiting list once the plots are cleared.
- Beatrix: contact the local radio station and the parish newsletter about the Open Day.
- Greta: draft the scarecrow competition rules before the next meeting.
- Ivo: buy and fit the combination lock.

Next meeting: Wednesday 2 July, 18:30, same room.

Addendum, added by Mei-Lin on 12 June: Samir obtained a lower quote of 655 for the four rainwater tanks with guttering, and the committee approved it by email. Separately, the Open Day budget was raised to 350 after Beatrix found that printing the posters would cost more than expected. The date and times of the Open Day are unchanged.
passages.p06:
ORRIN HX-3 CONICAL BURR GRINDER - USER MANUAL (EXCERPT)
Model: HX-3. Firmware: 2.4. Manufactured by Orrin Appliances.

Safety. Always unplug the grinder before removing the upper burr or cleaning the chute. Do not grind anything other than roasted coffee beans: no spices, rice, nuts, or frozen beans. Do not operate the grinder for more than 90 seconds continuously; after 90 seconds of grinding, allow at least 3 minutes to cool before the next cycle. Keep the grinder and its cable out of reach of children under 8.

Specifications. Power: 150 W. Voltage: 220 to 240 V. Weight: 3.2 kg. Height: 38 cm. The HX-3 has a 250 g bean hopper, a 54 mm conical steel burr set, a grind cup holding up to 60 g of ground coffee, a portafilter cradle, a dial with 40 grind settings, and a small display showing time.

Grind settings. Setting 1 is the finest and setting 40 is the coarsest. Recommended starting points:
- Espresso: settings 4 to 10
- Moka pot: settings 11 to 15
- Pour-over and drip: settings 18 to 26
- French press: settings 30 to 36
- Cold brew: settings 37 to 40
Change the setting only while the motor is running or the hopper is empty, to avoid trapping beans between the burrs. Fresher beans usually need a slightly coarser setting than older beans.

Dosing modes. The grinder has three modes, selected with the MODE button:
- Timed mode: grinds for a set time, adjustable from 1.0 to 60.0 seconds in steps of 0.1 seconds.
- Single and Double presets: default times of 9.5 seconds and 17.0 seconds. Either preset can be changed by holding its button for 3 seconds and then turning the dial.
- Manual mode: grinds only while the START button is held down.
The display shows the dose time, not the weight. The HX-3 does not weigh coffee; for accurate weight, use a separate scale. As a rough guide, at setting 8 the grinder produces about 1.1 g of ground coffee per second. At coarser settings it produces more per second.

Cleaning. Brush out the chute after each day's use. Every two weeks, remove the upper burr (turn the dial anticlockwise past setting 40 until the burr releases) and brush both burrs. Never wash the burrs in water. Once a month, run 30 g of grinder cleaning tablets through the grinder at setting 20, then grind about 20 g of coffee and discard it. Do not use rice as a cleaner; it can damage the motor and is not covered by the warranty.

Error codes.
- E1: Hopper not seated. Push the hopper down and turn it clockwise until it clicks.
- E2: Motor overheated. Unplug the grinder and allow 20 minutes to cool.
- E3: Burr jam. Unplug, empty the hopper, remove the upper burr and clear the obstruction.
- E4: Grind cup missing. Place the grind cup or a portafilter in the cradle.
- E5: Firmware error. Hold MODE and START together for 10 seconds to restart. If E5 returns, contact support.
If E2 appears more than three times in one week, stop using the grinder and contact support.

Troubleshooting.
- Grinder runs but no coffee comes out: the hopper may be empty, or beans may be bridging in the hopper. Tap the hopper gently.
- Coffee clumps in the grind cup: this is normal at espresso settings. Stir with a fine needle or shake the cup gently.
- Grinder is louder than usual: check for a stone or foreign object and follow the steps for E3.
- Display does not light up: check the plug and the fuse. The fuse is rated at 3 A.
- Grind size seems inconsistent from day to day: the burrs may need cleaning, or the dial may have been turned while beans were trapped between the burrs. Clean the burrs as described in the Cleaning section and re-check your setting with a fresh dose.

Warranty. The HX-3 has a 2-year warranty from the date of purchase, covering defects in materials and workmanship. The warranty is extended to 3 years if the product is registered at orrin-appliances.example within 30 days of purchase. The burrs are treated as wear parts and are covered for 1 year only, whether or not the product is registered. The warranty does not cover damage caused by grinding anything other than coffee beans, by dropping the unit, or by fitting unofficial replacement burrs. Keep your proof of purchase.

Replacement parts. Replacement burr set: part HX-B54, price 34. Grind cup: part HX-C60, price 12. Hopper lid: part HX-L1, price 6. Cleaning brush: part HX-BR, price 4. Order from the Orrin website or an authorised dealer.

Changes in firmware 2.4. This version changes the default Double preset time from 17.0 seconds to 18.5 seconds; the default Single preset time is unchanged. It also adds a low-bean warning: if the grinder detects that the hopper runs empty during a timed dose, the display flashes and the remaining time is paused until START is pressed again.
passages.p07:
A Short History of Wrenholt

Wrenholt began as a ferry crossing on the River Tamble. The first written record of the settlement is a toll list from 1612, which names a ferryman called Aldous Crane and sets a charge of a halfpenny for each person and a penny for each horse. For most of the seventeenth century, Wrenholt was little more than the ferry house, an inn called the Drowned Lantern, and a handful of cottages.

The town grew after 1738, when the merchant Honora Lisle built a stone quay and a warehouse for the wool trade. By 1760 there were four warehouses on the quay, and the population had risen to about 600. The first bridge across the Tamble, a wooden trestle bridge, was built in 1771 and ended the ferry service. It was paid for by a toll on every crossing.

In 1802 a flood destroyed the wooden bridge and two of the four warehouses. The replacement, a five-arch stone bridge designed by the engineer Silas Marwood, opened in 1806. The bridge toll was finally abolished in 1829. Marwood's bridge still stands, although its central arch had to be rebuilt in 1954 after it was struck by a runaway barge.

The railway reached Wrenholt in 1847, when the town's first station was built on the east bank. The wool trade declined in the second half of the nineteenth century, but two new industries replaced it: a brickworks, opened by the Faraday-Stone family in 1859, and a paper mill, opened in 1868. At its peak in 1901, the brickworks employed 340 people, making it the largest employer in the town. The census that year recorded a population of 7,420.

Wrenholt became a borough in 1874. Its first mayor was Edmund Faraday-Stone, owner of the brickworks. The town hall on Market Square was completed in 1881 and still houses the town council today. The clock in the town hall tower was added in 1890, paid for by public subscription. It is known locally as "Old Tuesday", because it was first started on a Tuesday, a day earlier than the ceremony planned for it.

The twentieth century brought both decline and renewal. The paper mill closed in 1931. The brickworks survived until 1978. The station on the east bank closed in 1966, and the old station building became the Wrenholt Museum in 1972. A new station, Wrenholt Parkway, opened on the west bank in 1994.

The first woman to serve as mayor of Wrenholt was Agnes Pollard, elected in 1936. She is best remembered for founding the town's public library in 1938, in a building donated by the Lisle family trust.

Today Wrenholt has a population of about 18,300, according to the most recent council estimate. The former brickworks site is now the Claypits Nature Reserve, opened in 1989, and the quay warehouses have been converted into flats and artists' studios. Each September the town holds the Lantern Fair, which commemorates the old ferry and ends with a procession of lanterns across Marwood's bridge.
passages.p08:
FERNMOOR PUBLIC LIBRARY - BORROWING RULES

Membership. Membership is free for anyone who lives, works, or studies in the Fernmoor district. Members must show their library card to borrow items. A replacement card costs 3.00. Junior membership is for children under 16.

Loan limits and loan periods.
- Adult members may borrow up to 12 items at a time.
- Junior members may borrow up to 8 items at a time.
- Books: 3 weeks.
- Audiobooks and music CDs: 3 weeks.
- DVDs and Blu-ray discs: 1 week.
- Board games: 2 weeks, with a maximum of 1 board game per member at a time.
- Reference books, newspapers and the local history collection may not be borrowed and must be used in the library.
- Laptops may be borrowed by adult members for use inside the library only, for up to 3 hours.

Renewals. Books, audiobooks and CDs can be renewed up to 2 times, online, by phone or at the desk, unless another member has reserved them. DVDs and board games cannot be renewed.

Reservations. Reserving an item costs 0.50, except for junior members and for items in the children's collection, which are free to reserve. Reserved items are kept at the desk for 7 days after the member is notified.

Overdue charges. Overdue books, audiobooks and CDs borrowed by adult members are charged at 0.20 per item per day, up to a maximum of 6.00 per item. Overdue DVDs and Blu-ray discs are charged at 1.00 per item per day, up to a maximum of 10.00 per item. Overdue board games are charged at 0.50 per day with no maximum. Junior members pay no overdue charges on any item. Members with 10.00 or more in unpaid charges cannot borrow until the charges are paid.

Lost or damaged items. The member pays the replacement cost shown in the library catalogue plus a processing fee of 2.50.

Opening hours. Monday to Friday 09:00 to 19:00, Saturday 09:00 to 16:00, closed on Sundays. The library is also closed on public holidays. Items due on a day when the library is closed may be returned on the next opening day without charge.
passages.p09:
Harlow Vale Five-a-Side Winter League - End of Season Report

The winter league ran from 5 November to 18 February with six teams, each playing every other team twice, for ten matches per team. All matches were played on Tuesday evenings at the Harlow Vale Leisure Centre. Three points were awarded for a win, one for a draw, and none for a loss.

The table below shows the results as played. It does not include the points deduction or the appeal described later in this report.

Final table as played (won-drawn-lost, goals for-against, points):
1. Copper Kites: 7-2-1, 31-14, 23 points
2. Northgate Rovers: 6-3-1, 28-15, 21 points
3. Lamplight FC: 5-2-3, 24-20, 17 points
4. Mill Street Athletic: 3-3-4, 19-21, 12 points
5. Bramble United: 2-2-6, 15-26, 8 points
6. Old Foundry: 0-2-8, 10-31, 2 points

Awards. The top scorer was Dario Lemm of Copper Kites with 14 goals, two more than Northgate's Yusuf Adair. The goalkeeper award went to Keeley Strand of Northgate Rovers, who kept five clean sheets. The fair play award went to Mill Street Athletic, who received only two yellow cards all season.

Disciplinary matters. On 30 January, the league committee found that Lamplight FC had fielded an unregistered player in two matches. The committee deducted 3 points from Lamplight FC's total; the results of those matches stand.

Appeal. Northgate Rovers appealed the result of their match against Copper Kites on 14 January, which had finished as a 2-2 draw, because Copper Kites had fielded a player who was serving a suspension. On 25 February, after the table above was first published, the committee upheld the appeal and awarded Northgate Rovers a 3-0 win in that match. All other results stand.

Prizes. The league champion receives the Harlow Vale Shield and 150 for team funds. The runner-up receives 75. Prizes will be presented at the spring league launch evening.

Spring league. Registration for the spring league closes on 10 March. The fee is 90 per team, reduced to 60 for teams that played the full winter season. The spring league will use the same rules, with one change: matches will be 25 minutes each way instead of 20.

The committee thanks the leisure centre staff and referees Olu Barnes and Petra Sand for their help throughout the season.
passages.p10:
QUILLON ROBOTICS - ANNUAL LEAVE AND TIME OFF POLICY (version 3)
Approved by Ines Carvalho, Head of People

1. Entitlement. Full-time employees receive 25 days of paid annual leave per leave year, plus public holidays. The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March. After 5 complete years of service, the entitlement rises to 27 days; after 10 complete years of service, it rises to 30 days.

2. Part-time employees. Part-time employees receive leave in proportion to the number of days they work each week, compared with a five-day full-time week, based on the entitlement for their length of service. For example, an employee working 3 days a week receives 3/5 of the matching full-time entitlement. Where this does not give a whole or half day, the result is rounded up to the nearest half day.

3. New starters and leavers. Employees who join or leave part-way through the leave year receive a proportion of their entitlement based on the number of complete months worked in that leave year.

4. Booking leave. Leave must be requested through the HR portal and approved by the employee's line manager. Requests for 1 or 2 days need at least 1 week's notice. Requests for 3 or more consecutive days need at least 4 weeks' notice. No more than 15 consecutive working days may be taken at once without approval from the Head of People.

5. Blackout periods. Leave cannot normally be taken during the last two weeks of March (the year-end stock count) or during the week of the Riverside Trade Expo each October. Exceptions may be approved by a director for bereavement, medical reasons, or weddings booked before the blackout dates were announced.

6. Carry-over. Up to 5 unused days may be carried over into the next leave year. Carried-over days must be used by 30 June, or they are lost. Employees returning from parental leave may carry over all of their unused days.

7. Buying and selling leave. Employees may buy up to 5 extra days of leave each leave year through salary sacrifice. Selling leave back to the company is not permitted, except for leavers, who are paid for leave that has been accrued but not taken.

8. Other paid time off.
- Bereavement: up to 5 days for a close family member; 1 day for others.
- Volunteering: 2 days per leave year for registered volunteering.
- Moving house: 1 day per leave year.
- Jury service: full salary for up to 10 working days, then the statutory rate.
- Birthday: every employee receives their birthday off, or the next working day if the birthday falls on a weekend or public holiday.

9. Sickness during leave. If an employee is ill during annual leave and provides a doctor's note, the affected days are treated as sick leave and the annual leave is returned to them.

10. Changes from version 2. This policy replaces version 2. The main changes are that the entitlement after 10 complete years of service has increased from 28 to 30 days, and the volunteering allowance has increased from 1 day to 2 days per leave year.
